summary: An unfinished 'Friends of Google Fonts' microsite for Crimson Pro (variable wght 200–900) built as a book: every section is a two-page spread with page numbers and running heads (intro, design, preview, acknowledgement) on a dark desk, themed on Alice in Wonderland ('Drink me', 'Eat me', 'White Rabbit with pink eyes'), with weight sliders, size buttons and editable artefacts (dictionary entry, newspaper, manuscript). Placeholders ('TK', 'shapes go here', broken images) remain, and the 3D book cover at the top did not render in the capture.

instances.look: Captured as an empty dark-grey screen with a single white dot (a slider thumb); the HTML holds a CSS 3D book: front cover 'Crimson Pro / is a variable font / for book and digital production…', spine 'Crimson Pro' and back cover 'Additional Credits' (Google: Dave Crossland, Irin Kim, Paula Ashton; site: Amélie Lamont)
instances.ux: A range input (wght 200–900, default 200) beside the book likely changes the cover's weight and/or turns the book; nothing rendered in headless capture
instances.learn: Open a specimen with the font as a physical book object: the cover, spine and back carry the intro and credits

reconstruction.layout: Full viewport (~916px) dark #262626; book with front, back, left (spine) and right faces in CSS 3D, centred; slider at the top-left (white thumb visible at x≈40, y≈120)
reconstruction.typography: Cover heading ~40px Crimson Pro, subheading italic, copy ~16px; spine title vertical
reconstruction.behaviour: input.slider.slider--book (200–900) → font-variation-settings on the cover (likely) and/or rotateY of .book
